status_rule: observed = opcode/id occurs in exactly one statement mapped by source order and handler/arg shape agrees

id_space_note.statement: The 0x49 id space is per exe: ids are keys of that exe's own res9 table (QM 2.4.2 and 2.4.12 builds number the same functions differently; ids 5, 6, 71, 78 happen to coincide).
id_space_note.evidence: res9 dumps (analysis/res9_tables.json). Same functions: QM 2.4.2 original-1 221/223/224/225/362/406/501/503 = GetLastError/OpenProcess/TerminateProcess/CloseHandle/GetStateTextW/WTSTerminateProcess/IsHungWindow/ProcessNameToId; 2.4.12 sample26 232/234/235/236/426/195(IsHungAppWindow)/523 + 584 __WinTest; sample02 380 = GetStateTextW.
id_space_note.consequence: qmdec names every 0x49 call from the exe's own res9; the previous +11/+18/+20 shift heuristic and the inferred 503 mapping are removed (the shifts were only the visible effect of different tables, not a rule). The earlier claim that the table lives in qm.exe is DROPPED: it is in each exe's resources 8/9.

res9_mechanism.layout: PE resource name 8 = u16 count + count NUL-terminated dll names (an empty name is a valid entry); resource 9 = u16 count + entries {u16 id, u16 dll (low 15 bits = index into res8; 0x8000 = flag, e.g. 32771 = dll 3 + flag), name NUL}; resource 10 (sample25 only) = u16 count + 8-byte records {u16 id, u16 0, u16 type, u16 0} = hidden global variables read by opcode 0x20.
res9_mechanism.evidence: handler 0x429650 -> 0x429520 -> 0x4294d0 looks the u16 id of opcode 0x49 up in the table built from res8/res9 at load; GetProcAddress resolves it (validator handler re-read + res9 dumps of all 31 exes, parsed by qmtool.parse_res8/9/10; audit_level1.py checks framing).
